london.name: London System
london.summary: An easy setup to remember: you play nearly the same moves almost every time, whatever your opponent does.

london-l01.title: The idea of the London System

london-l01-s01.text: As White, you almost always play the same structure: pawns on d4, e3 and c3, with the dark-squared bishop outside the chain on f4.

london-l01-s02.text: This is the full setup. The bishop comes out before you close the pawn chain with e3.

london-l01-s03.text: The plan: bring out the bishop, close with e3, develop the knights, castle and aim the knight at e5.

london-l01-s04.prompt: Which bishop should you bring out before playing e3?
london-l01-s04.explanation: If you play e3 first, the c1 bishop gets shut in behind your own pawns.
options: The c1 bishop, on the dark squares
The f1 bishop, on the light squares

london-l01-s05.prompt: What is the correct order of the first moves?
london-l01-s05.explanation: First the queen's pawn, then the bishop out, and finally e3.

italian.name: Italian Game
italian.summary: Quick development, a bishop aimed at f7 and a clear plan: castle and take the center.

italian-l01.title: The idea of the Italian
italian-l01.summary: Bishop to c4 and solid play

italian-l01-s01.text: The c4 bishop aims at f7, the weakest point in Black's camp: at first, only the king protects it.

italian-l01-s02.text: In the quiet version, c3 and d3 form a solid base. Then you castle and choose between d4 or regrouping your knights.

italian-l01-s03.prompt: Which point does the c4 bishop attack?
italian-l01-s03.explanation: The f7-pawn is protected only by the king.

italian-l01-s04.prompt: What does the move c3 prepare?
italian-l01-s04.explanation: With c3, the d4-pawn will have support when you play it.
options: The d4 advance to take the center

vienna.name: Vienna Game
vienna.summary: A flexible opening: you can attack with the f4 gambit or pressure f7 with your bishop.

vienna-l01.title: The idea of the Vienna
vienna-l01.summary: Knight to c3 and two plans

vienna-l01-s01.text: With 2.Nc3 you develop a piece, protect e4 and keep the choice between two plans open: the gambit with f4 or Bc4.

vienna-l01-s02.text: With f4 you attack Black's center and open the f-file. The cost: you weaken the diagonal from e1 to h4.

vienna-l01-s03.prompt: Which pawn do you sacrifice in the Vienna Gambit?
vienna-l01-s03.explanation: You offer the f4-pawn to open lines and attack the center.

vienna-l01-s04.prompt: Which diagonal does the move f4 weaken?
vienna-l01-s04.explanation: A queen check on h4 can come along that diagonal.
options: The one from e1 to h4
The one from a1 to h8
The one from a2 to g8

scandinavian.name: Scandinavian Defense
scandinavian.summary: You challenge White's center from the very first move, with a simple plan and few lines to memorize.

scandinavian-l01.title: The idea of the Scandinavian
scandinavian-l01.summary: Attacking the center from the start

scandinavian-l01-s01.text: With ...d5 you attack White's center right away and force White to decide.

scandinavian-l01-s02.text: The queen comes out early, but it retreats to a5 with tempo and pins the c3 knight when the diagonal opens.

scandinavian-l01-s03.text: The plan: ...c6 to support the center, the bishop out before ...e6, the knight to f6 and kingside castling.

scandinavian-l01-s04.prompt: Which bishop should you bring out before playing ...e6?
scandinavian-l01-s04.explanation: If you play ...e6 first, the c8 bishop gets shut in behind your pawns.
options: The c8 bishop, on the light squares
The f8 bishop, on the dark squares

sicilian.name: Sicilian Defense (Najdorf)
sicilian.summary: The most combative answer to 1.e4: an unbalanced structure and playing to win with Black.

sicilian-l01.title: The idea of the Sicilian
sicilian-l01.summary: Imbalance and the fight for d4

sicilian-l01-s01.text: With ...c5 you don't copy White: you fight for the d4 square from the side.

sicilian-l01-s02.text: You trade your c-pawn for White's central pawn. After that, you have more pawns in the center and White has more on the queenside.

sicilian-l01-s03.text: A typical position: you have a comfortable center with ...e5, and White attacks your king with f3, Qd2 and queenside castling. Your play is on the queenside.

sicilian-l01-s04.prompt: What do you trade in the Sicilian?
sicilian-l01-s04.explanation: The trade ...cxd4 draws away White's central pawn and leaves you with more central pawns.

sicilian-l01-s05.prompt: What is ...a6 for in the Najdorf?
sicilian-l01-s05.explanation: It stops a white bishop or knight from reaching b5 and prepares the queenside advance.
